text:
sophia: Heads up — quickstart shell snippet in README breaks if folks copy it from Windows. Repro + quick fixes below.

kevin: ugh yeah we saw one customer hit this yesterday, error was 'bash: /tmp/quickstart.sh: /bin/bash^M: bad interpreter: No such file or directory' right?

sophia: exactly. root cause: the snippet got CRLFs and the original shebang was missing the env form. The README currently has:
```
#!/bin/bash
curl -s https://api.redwood.ai/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
but when copy-pasted from GH on Windows it becomes `#!/bin/bash\r` and fails. Also on mac/linux we prefer `#!/usr/bin/env bash` so it works in more shells.

aj: quick repro steps I used: 1) copy snippet on Windows machine 2) paste into notepad -> save as quickstart.sh 3) scp to linux box 4) run `bash quickstart.sh` -> boom.

maya: workaround for now: tell people to run `dos2unix quickstart.sh` or `sed -i 's/\r$//' quickstart.sh` and `chmod +x quickstart.sh`. Want me to add a note in the README?

sophia: yes please. Also we should change snippet to: 
```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
and in the markdown mention Windows users: use the PowerShell example below or run `dos2unix`.

kevin: add PS sample too. Folks on Windows are copying the bash example and then wondering why it fails. A simple PS snippet like: 
```powershell
$body = @{ prompt = 'hi' } | ConvertTo-Json
Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' -Method Post -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $env:REDWOOD_KEY" } -Body $body -ContentType 'application/json'
```
should be good.

aj: also noticed the README code block lacked triple backticks fence language in one spot, GH rendered it fine but some copy-paste tools strip the shebang. We should add a small callout: "Copying scripts? Use raw view or download".

sophia: I can open a tiny PR with three changes: use /usr/bin/env shebang, add `set -euo pipefail`, add the PowerShell snippet and a note about CRLFs.

devex-bot: PR template reminder — add a short changelog line and run docs link check.

maya: also add a tiny test in CI that checks shell snippets for CRLF and ensures shebang is present. I can sketch a GH action: `find docs -name '*.md' -exec grep -n "#!" {} \;` then verify no CRLFs.

sophia: great idea — prevents regression. I'll file the PR and link it here. Thanks! :pray:
